causes.label: Some of the sounds you’ll hear are normal
remedies: Detergent cup opening.
The motor starting during the drying period.
Water draining out of the tub immediately after you start the dishwasher.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Some of the sounds you’ll hear are normal"

causes.label: Utensils are not secure in the rack or something small has dropped into the rack
remedies: Make sure everything is secured in dishwasher.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Utensils are not secure in the rack or something small has dropped into the rack"

causes.label: Motor hums
remedies: Dishwasher has not been used on a regular basis.
If you do not use your dishwasher often, set it to fill and pump out once every week.
This will help keep the seal moist.
Dishwasher control was not advanced properly to the start of the desired cycle.
Advance the control to the start of the desired cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Motor hums"

causes.label: Dishes are blocking the detergent cups
remedies: Reposition the dishes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Dishes are blocking the detergent cups"

symptoms.symptom: Water standing in the bottom of the tub

causes.label: Drain is clogged
remedies: If you have an air gap, clean it.
Check to see if your kitchen sink is draining well.
If not, you may need a plumber.
If the dishwasher drains into a disposer, run disposer clear.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Drain is clogged"

causes.label: This is normal
remedies: A small amount of clean water around the outlet of the tub bottom at the back of the tub keeps the water seal lubricated.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "This is normal"

causes.label: Correct detergent wasn’t used
remedies: Use only automatic dishwasher detergents to avoid sudsing.
Cascade® Dishwashing Detergent has been approved for use in all GE dishwashers.
To remove suds from the tub, open the dishwasher and let suds evaporate.
Add 1 gallon of cold water to the tub.
Close and latch the dishwasher.
Repeat if necessary.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Correct detergent wasn’t used"

causes.label: Rinse agent was spilled
remedies: Always wipe up rinse agent spills immediately.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Rinse agent was spilled"

causes.label: Detergent with colorant was used
remedies: Some detergents contain colorant (pigment or dyes) that will discolor the tub interior with extended use.
Check the detergent cup for signs of any discoloration.
If cup is discolored, change to detergent without any colorant.
Cascade® Dishwashing Detergents has been approved for use in all GE dishwashers.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Detergent with colorant was used"

causes.label: Some tomato-based foods can stain
remedies: Use of the RINSE ONLY cycle after adding the dish to the load can decrease the level of staining.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Some tomato-based foods can stain"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is correct (see page 6).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Low inlet water temperature"

symptoms.symptom: Spots and filming on glasses and flatware

causes.label: Extremely hard water
remedies: Use Cascade Crystal Clear® rinse agent to remove spots and prevent new film buildup.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Extremely hard water"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure water temperature is at least 120°F.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Old or damp powder detergent
remedies: Make sure detergent is fresh.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Old or damp powder detergent"

symptoms.symptom: Cloudiness on glassware black or gray marks on dishes

causes.label: Combination of soft water and too much detergent
remedies: This is called etching and is permanent.
To prevent this from happening, use less detergent if you have soft water.
Wash glassware in the shortest cycle that will get them clean.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Combination of soft water and too much detergent"

causes.label: Water temperature entering the dishwasher exceeds 150°F
remedies: Lower the water heater temperature.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Water temperature entering the dishwasher exceeds 150°F"

causes.label: Aluminum utensils have rubbed against dishes
remedies: Remove marks with a mild, abrasive cleaner.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Aluminum utensils have rubbed against dishes"

symptoms.symptom: Yellow or brown film on inside surfaces

causes.label: Tea or coffee stains
remedies: Remove the stain by hand, using a solution of 1/2 cup bleach and 3 cups warm water.
WARNING before cleaning interior wait at least 20 minutes after a cycle for the heating element to cool down.
Failure to do so can result in burns.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Tea or coffee stains"

causes.label: Hard water minerals
remedies: To clean the interior, apply dishwasher detergent to a damp sponge.
Wear rubber gloves.
Do not use any type of cleanser other than dishwasher detergent because it may cause foaming or sudsing.
Cascade® Automatic Dishwashing Detergent has been approved for use in all GE dishwashers.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Hard water minerals"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is correct (see page 6).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Rinse agent dispenser is empty
remedies: Check the rinse agent dispenser.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Rinse agent dispenser is empty"

causes.label: Fuse is blown, or the circuit breaker tripped
remedies: Replace fuse or reset circuit breaker.
Remove any other appliances from the circuit.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Fuse is blown, or the circuit breaker tripped"

causes.label: Power is turned off
remedies: In some installations, the power to the dishwasher is proved through a wall switch, often located next to the disposer switch.

causes.label: Reboot your control
remedies: Turn off power to the dishwasher (at circuit breaker or wall switch) for 30 seconds, then turn back on.
